description: Source credibility registry for Disaster Info Verification System

credibility_tiers.A: Official government or intergovernmental agency (UN, NDMA, national meteorological service). Highest authority.
credibility_tiers.B: Established humanitarian organization with verified operations (ReliefWeb, OCHA, Red Cross). High credibility.
credibility_tiers.C: Credible news media or verified research publication. Medium credibility — verify with Tier A/B where possible.
credibility_tiers.D: Social media, unverified reports, crowdsourced. Low credibility — use as claims only, not as authoritative evidence.

sources.source_name: GDACS — Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
sources.notes: Run by European Commission and UN OCHA. Provides GeoJSON and RSS feeds of active/recent disasters worldwide. Public feed does not require registration.

Managed by OCHA. Public REST API available at https://apidoc.reliefweb.int — no key required for basic access. Provides humanitarian situation reports, disaster updates with country, date, and event type metadata.

sources.license: REQUIRES_HUMAN_ACCEPTANCE — research dataset, terms at source URL
sources.notes: Social-media posts (Twitter) about disasters, annotated for informativeness and humanitarian categories. Use as CLAIMS source only, NOT as authoritative evidence. Requires manual download after accepting terms.

sources.source_name: NDMA — National Disaster Management Authority India
sources.license: REQUIRES_REVIEW — Indian government open data policy
sources.notes: Official Indian disaster management authority. No stable public API known as of 2026-10. Access method requires human evaluation — web scraping legality must be confirmed. Covers India-specific disasters only.
